# Every issue a spreadsheet can raise

Every problem, question and note the change engine (`planChanges`, [the change engine](rules/change-engine.md)) raises has a **kind**, and its level is fixed by its kind ([kinds, levels and near misses](rules/import-levels.md)). This page lists every kind: what raises it (`src/domain/issueKinds.ts`), what its group says and the answers it takes, run on [its case in import.csv](../conformance/import.csv) (column `kinds` lists every kind a case raised). Then every other spelling a column or a word is read by. The columns themselves are in [the export format](export-format.md).

A group’s sentence counts its rows, so a file with more rows says the same with another number. A kind with no case is one the engine itself never raises: the table says what does instead.

## Must fix (`must`)

Faro can’t record it truthfully. Nothing is saved while one is left, unless an answer leaves its rows out.

| Kind | Raised when | What it says, in its case | Answers in the preview | Case in import.csv |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `required-empty` | A column a new row must have is empty: a goal’s name, owner, Start or Target, Limit or Stages for its type; a person’s name or email. | 1 new goal has no owner | — | `required-empty` |
| `not-a-number` | A number column holds text: “six”, “12 days”, an effect that isn’t a number. | 1 check-in has text where a number goes (Value) | — | `not-a-number` |
| `formula` | A number cell starts with “=”: a formula, not a number. | 1 cell holds a formula, not a number | — | `formula` |
| `precision` | A number has more decimal places than its goal keeps. | 1 number has more decimal places than its goal keeps | Keep 2 decimal places for this goal | `precision` |
| `impossible-number` | A number that can’t be right for its unit: below zero for a count, time, money or share; over 100 for a share. | 1 number can’t be right | — | `impossible-number` |
| `unknown-word` | A word column (Level, Type, Plan, Call, Cause…) holds a word it doesn’t know, with no near miss. | Level says “vp” on 1 row | Choose from the column’s words | `unknown-word` |
| `unknown-ref` | A person, team or goal that matches nothing here, with no near miss. | 1 row names a team that isn’t here: “Infra Guild” | Choose a team · Add Infra Guild as a new team | `unknown-ref` |
| `ambiguous-ref` | A name that two or more people or goals share, so which one is meant can’t be told. | 1 row say “Shared name”, and more than one goal is called that | Choose which | `ambiguous-ref` |
| `conflicting-refs` | Two columns that name the same thing disagree: Owner and Owner ID or Owner email; Feeds into and Feeds into key. | 1 row names two different people | — | `conflicting-refs` |
| `bad-key` | A key that isn’t one (“12”), or a key or ID that matches no goal in this cycle (G-999). | 1 key doesn’t look like G-12 | — | `bad-key` |
| `duplicate` | One goal, person, or goal and week, on two rows of one sheet. | 2 goals appear on more than one row | Use the last row for each · Use the first | `duplicate` |
| `type-unclear` | A new goal with no Type that fills in none, or more than one, of the type groups (Start and Target; Limit; Stages). | 1 new goal doesn’t say what type it is | Choose a type | `type-unclear` |
| `plan-order` | A plan that ends before it starts, or a plan week outside the plan; a To before its From. | 1 plan ends before it starts, or has weeks outside it | — | `plan-order` |
| `stage-format` | A stage with no name or no week (“Design” with no @week), a week past the cycle, or one name twice. | 1 row has stages that can’t be read | — | `stage-format` |
| `week-wrong` | A check-in for week 0, a week that hasn’t happened, or no week that can be read; a goal year’s week that doesn’t exist. | 1 check-in is for weeks that haven’t happened | — | `week-wrong` |
| `checkin-incomplete` | A check-in the check-in screen would not post: behind plan with no cause or why, off track with no path to green, a better call with no reason. | 1 check-in needs a Path to green and, if it’s a plan, Back on plan by week (after week 45, by week 53) | — | `checkin-incomplete` |
| `cant-change` | A row changes something that never changes: an existing goal’s Type, a check-in’s week, an email taken away, a goal this file also stops. | 1 row changes something that can’t change | — | `cant-change` |
| `not-allowed` | The person loading the file may not make the change: a goal they don’t own and aren’t an admin for, people when they aren’t an admin, a goal at a level only its owner may set. | 1 row changes a goal you don’t own | Leave these rows out | `not-allowed` |
| `removal-refused` | Stop with no reason, Delete on a goal with check-ins, or Left with no one to take over. | 1 row can’t be stopped or deleted as it stands | — | `removal-refused` |
| `loop` | A goal that would feed itself, directly or round a loop of Feeds into links. | 1 goal would feed itself | — | `loop` |

## Check (`check`)

Possible but unlikely: a question. The change saves once it is answered; one answer covers every row in its group.

| Kind | Raised when | What it says, in its case | Answers in the preview | Case in import.csv |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `near-ref` | A person, team, goal or stage name within reach of exactly one that is here (one edit under 8 folded characters, two from 8). | 1 row names a team that isn’t here: “CI/DC”. Did you mean CI/CD? | Use CI/CD · Add CI/DC as a new team · Choose another | `near-ref` |
| `near-word` | A word column’s word within reach of exactly one of its words or their other spellings. | Type says “numbr” on 1 row. Read it as number? | Read it as number · Choose another | `near-word` |
| `near-header` | A header within reach of exactly one of the sheet’s columns or their other names (“Targett”). | A column on Goals is called “targett”. Read it as Target? | Read it as Target · Don’t read it | `near-header` |
| `two-columns` | Two headers on one sheet read as the same column (“Goal” and “Goal name”): which to read is asked, neither dropped quietly. | Two columns on Goals are read as Goal: “goal” and “goal name”. Which should be read? | Read “goal” · Read “goal name” | `two-columns` |
| `new-team` | A team that isn’t here, with no near miss, in an admin’s file. | — | — | None. Not raised as its own question: an admin settles an unknown team with unknown-ref’s or near-ref’s “Add as a new team” answer. |
| `same-person` | A new person whose name is, or is one edit from, someone’s here: the same person, or someone new? | “Rhea Kapor” (rhea.k@example.com) looks like Rhea Kapoor (CI/CD), who is already here. | The same person: give Rhea Kapoor this email · Someone new | `same-person` |
| `same-goal` | A new goal with a name its team already has (or a goal with no team has). | 1 new goal has a name its team already uses: “Pipeline queue wait (p90)”. Are they new? | They’re new goals · They’re the same: change G-14 · Leave them out | `same-goal` |
| `other-goal` | A row’s key matches a goal, but its name, owner and team all differ from that goal’s. | G-1 is “Lead time for changes” here, owned by Rhea Kapoor. Row 2 calls it “Net revenue retention”. Is it the same goal? | Yes, change it · No, add it as a new goal · Leave it out | `other-goal` |
| `other-workspace` | The file’s Start here sheet carries another workspace’s id. | — | — | None. Asked by the import screen before the engine runs (src/modules/spreadsheets/importPlan.ts): answered “Add its rows as new goals”, the keys and IDs are dropped and the engine sees new rows. |
| `past-stage` | A new goal’s stage is due before this week. | 1 new goal has stages due before this week. Are they done? | They’re done · They’re not done · Count them from this week | `past-stage` |
| `past-plan` | A new number goal whose plan ended before this week. | 1 new goal has a plan that has already ended | They’re finished goals: add them · Leave them out | `past-plan` |
| `odd-number` | A number the goal form would ask about: a hundred times the start, a share over 100 when it isn’t one, a typed unit that isn’t the goal’s, a value far from the last. | The target (3,000 ms) is over 100 times where it starts (3 ms). Is that right? | They’re right · Leave these rows out | `odd-number` |
| `plan-question` | A change to an existing goal’s plan that turns its direction round, or moves its target far. | This makes higher better: the target (80 hours) is now above the start (52 hours). It was 52 hours to 24 hours, lower is better. | Yes, make higher better · Leave these rows out | `plan-question` |
| `no-unit` | A new number or range goal with no unit, or an existing goal’s unit cleared. | 1 new goal has no unit, so its numbers will show bare. Is it a plain count? | That’s right · Leave them out | `no-unit` |
| `decimal-comma` | A number read with a comma as its decimal mark (“1,5” as 1.5). | 1 number uses a comma as the decimal mark. “1,5” was read as 1.5: a comma as the decimal mark. Is that right? | That’s right · Leave these rows out | `decimal-comma` |
| `replaces-others` | Ten or more rows replace check-ins other people posted. | 10 rows replace check-ins other people posted | Replace them · Leave these rows out | `replaces-others` |
| `many-admins` | Three or more people become admins. | 3 people would become admins | That’s right · Leave these rows out | `many-admins` |
| `totals-row` | A row called Total, Totals or Sum with no owner. | Row 2 is called “TOTAL” and has no owner. It looks like a totals row. | Leave it out · It’s a goal | `totals-row` |
| `big-removal` | Five or more rows say Stop, Delete or Left. | This file stops 5 goals. Is that right? | That’s right · Leave these rows out | `big-removal` |
| `feeds-lower` | A goal that feeds a goal at a lower level than its own. | A north star usually feeds nothing, and “Pipeline queue wait (p90)” is an SVP goal. Is this link right? | Yes, it feeds that goal · Leave these rows out | `feeds-lower` |
| `for-someone-else` | New goals for other people with no State: asked once per file whether they start active or proposed (GE10, decision 16). Set-up never asks; confirm answers active. | One of these goals is for other people and would start as active. Is that what you mean? | Yes, active · No, start them as proposed | `for-someone-else` |

## Read as (`note`)

How a row was read. Said on the change, never a block.

| Kind | Raised when | What it says, in its case | Answers in the preview | Case in import.csv |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `by-name` | An owner or person given by name alone, matched to exactly one person (an email column is exact). | “Rhea Kapoor” matched by name: Rhea Kapoor. An email column is exact. | — | `required-empty-start` |
| `default` | A cell left empty on a new goal, filled with its default: the owner’s team, or the type read from the columns filled in. | Team: CI/CD (the owner’s team; the row gave none). | — | `required-empty-start` |
| `date-as-week` | A date in a week column, read as the week of the cycle it falls in. | “2026-11-04” was read as week 45. | — | `date-as-week` |
| `folded` | A name matched only once folded (“ci cd” as CI/CD). | — | — | None. Not raised: a name that folds equal to one here is read as it, without a word. |
| `same-name` | A new goal or person that shares a name with one here, which is allowed: two teams may both have “Reduce latency”; at set-up, the email says who someone is. | Another goal is called “Pipeline queue wait (p90)” (G-14, CI/CD). That’s allowed; Faro shows each one’s key beside the title so people can tell them apart. | — | `same-goal` |
| `left-alone` | A row for a goal stopped before (a whole-cycle export carries them): its rows are left as they are. | “Pipeline queue wait (p90)” is stopped, so its rows are left as they are. | — | `left-alone` |
| `replaces` | A check-in row for a goal and week that already has one, which it replaces (fewer than ten of other people’s). | Replaces Rhea Kapoor’s check-in for week 41. | — | `replaces-others` |
| `as-recorded` | At set-up from another workspace’s export, a past week that today’s plan would ask more of, taken as it was written. | Week 20 is taken as it was recorded. | — | `as-recorded` |
| `example` | A row whose Action says Example. | — | — | None. Not raised: example rows are counted and skipped (the change set’s `examples`), never an issue. |


## Other names for a column

A header is read as its column when it is the column’s name or one of these, in any case. One within reach of exactly one of them is asked about (`near-header`); two headers read as one column are asked which (`two-columns`).

| Sheet | Column | Also read as |
|---|---|---|
| Goals | Goal | `goal name`, `title`, `objective` |
| Goals | Level | `goal level` |
| Goals | Team | `team name` |
| Goals | Owner | `owner name` |
| Goals | Owner email | `owner e-mail`, `owner email address` |
| Goals | Type | `goal type` |
| Goals | Unit | `units` |
| Goals | Start | `baseline` |
| Goals | Target | `target value`, `goal value` |
| Goals | From | `from week` |
| Goals | To | `to week` |
| Goals | Due week | `due`, `deadline week` |
| Goals | Reason | `reason for change` |

## Other spellings of a word

A word column reads its words, and these, in any case. The export writes the first. A word within reach of exactly one of all of them is asked about (`near-word`); any other is Must fix (`unknown-word`).

| Column | Word | Also read as |
|---|---|---|
| Level | `north star` | `northstar`, `headline`, `north star goal` |
| Level | `svp` | `senior vp`, `senior` |
| Type | `metric` | `move a number`, `number` |
| Type | `range` | `keep a number in range`, `keep in range` |
| Type | `milestone` | `hit dated stages`, `stages` |
| Plan | `straight` | `linear`, `straight line` |
| Plan | `back-loaded` | `back`, `backloaded`, `back loaded` |
| Plan | `stepped` | `steps`, `step` |
| Must stay | `at most` | `atmost`, `max`, `maximum`, `<=`, `≤`, `below` |
| Must stay | `at least` | `atleast`, `min`, `minimum`, `>=`, `≥`, `above` |
| Admin | `yes` | `y`, `true`, `1`, `x`, `admin` |
| Admin | `no` | `n`, `false`, `0` |
| Call | `On track` | `green` |
| Call | `At risk` | `amber`, `yellow` |
| Call | `Off track` | `red` |
| Recovery | `Needs a decision or help` | `help` |
| Recovery | `Target should change` | `target` |
| Action | `Stop` | `stopped` |
| Action | `Delete` | `deleted`, `remove` |
| Action | `Left` | `leave`, `leaving`, `mark as left` |
